answers.answer: Relationship SCOPe supports. In SCOPe 2.08 (current release; frozen 2021-07-28), the ubiquitin-related proteins, the UBX domains, and the Ras-binding domains are three sibling families within a single superfamily, d.15.1 'Ubiquitin-like' (sunid 54236), in fold d.15 'beta-Grasp (ubiquitin-like)' (sunid 54235), class d (alpha+beta). The families are d.15.1.1 'Ubiquitin-related' (sunid 54237; Pfam PF00240; members include ubiquitin, SUMO-1/2/3, Nedd8, Rub1, Elongin B, ISG15, Hub1, Ubl5, and the Ubl domains of Rad23, parkin, ubiquilins), d.15.1.2 'UBX domain' (sunid 54250; Pfam PF00789; p47, FAF1, Tug, UBXD6/Rep8, KIAA0794), and d.15.1.5 'Ras-binding domain, RBD' (sunid 54263; Pfam PF00788 + PF02196; c-Raf1 and A-Raf RBDs, RalGDS, Rlf, Rgl, RapGEF5, PI3K RBD, PLC-epsilon, Byr2, afadin, RASSF8, GRB7, RGS14). Placing them in one superfamily is SCOPe's assertion of probable common evolutionary origin: shared beta-grasp core with the ubiquitin beta-beta-alpha-beta-beta topology plus structural/sequence/functional features judged to exceed what fold-level convergence would explain. The biologically useful inference is therefore (a) homology of the domain scaffold, so the three families can be aligned structurally and the ubiquitin-like fold can be used to recognise the domain in new sequences or AlphaFold models, and (b) a shared mode of use as a compact protein-interaction module whose beta-sheet face (the ubiquitin Ile44-patch surface / RBD beta2 edge) mediates binding. The superfamily also holds other diverged families (GABARAP-like d.15.1.3, first domain of FERM d.15.1.4, APG12-like d.15.1.7, DIX d.15.1.8, viral protease Ubl d.15.1.9, Rho GTPase-binding domain d.15.1.10), underscoring that the superfamily is a scaffold-level, not a function-level, grouping. Note also that the fold d.15 contains 15 superfamilies (e.g. d.15.2 CAD & PB1, d.15.3 MoaD/ThiS, d.15.4 2Fe-2S ferredoxin-like, d.15.7 Ig-binding domains); fold-level sharing implies no homology claim at all, so MoaD/ThiS or ferredoxin-like domains must not be treated as ubiquitin relatives on SCOPe evidence. Unsafe annotation transfer. Family membership, not superfamily membership, is the only level at which SCOPe implies close enough relationship for function to be transferred, and even then only with sequence-level evidence. Specifically: (1) Do not transfer 'ubiquitin/Ubl modifier' function (conjugation via a C-terminal diglycine to E1/E2/E3 enzymes, isopeptide ligation to lysines, proteasome targeting, SUMOylation/NEDDylation) to UBX or RBD domains. UBX domains are not conjugated; they are integral domains of adaptor proteins (p47, FAF1, Tug) whose conserved function is binding the p97/VCP/Cdc48 ATPase N-domain, and they lack the C-terminal Gly-Gly. RBDs are not modifiers either; they are effector/regulator domains that bind GTP-loaded Ras-family small GTPases (Ras, Rap, Ral) via an intermolecular beta-sheet. (2) Do not transfer GTPase binding to ubiquitin-related or UBX proteins, nor p97 binding to ubiquitin or RBD proteins. (3) Do not assume the same binding surface or partner across families: the ubiquitin hydrophobic patch, the UBX S3/S4 loop that contacts p97-N, and the RBD beta1-beta2/alpha1 Ras-binding face are different residues on a homologous scaffold. (4) Within the RBD family itself, Ras-family specificity (Ras vs Rap vs Ral, Raf vs PI3K vs RalGDS) differs and cannot be read from SCOPe classification; it requires sequence identity to a characterised member, binding assays, or complex structures. (5) Within d.15.1.1, 'ubiquitin-related' includes non-conjugated Ubl domains (Rad23, parkin, ubiquilin, Elongin B, NUB1), so even same-family membership does not imply that a domain is a transferable modifier; the C-terminal diglycine and E1 specificity must be checked. (6) Template use: any d.15.1 member is an acceptable fold-level template for the beta-grasp core, but loop lengths, the extra N- or C-terminal elements, and the partner-binding faces vary by family, so interface modelling and docking should use a same-family template with demonstrable sequence similarity. (7) Representative selection: SCOPe's 'automated matches' protein nodes (sunids 190118, 191298, 190541) are assigned by sequence to existing families and carry no manual functional curation; and the 2.08 Pfam cross-references (PF00240, PF00789, PF00788/PF02196) are family-level, not superfamily-level, so Pfam-based function should also be transferred only within a family. Required external evidence for any functional claim beyond 'ubiquitin-like beta-grasp interaction domain': experimental partner identification (p97 binding, Ras-GTP binding, E1/E2 conjugation), the presence or absence of the C-terminal diglycine, and sequence-level similarity to a characterised family member.
